title: ADA Analysis Laboratory
description: ADA laboratory or facility building block. Extends the core CDIF spatialExtent (schema:Place) with a Wikidata laboratory classification via additionalType. Inherits place name, identifier, alternateName, geo coordinates, and geosparql geometry from spatialExtent.

schema:additionalType.description:
Must classify the place as a laboratory. The value is a sealed reference ({"@id": ...}) so JSON-LD expands it to a real IRI; written as a bare string it stays a literal that looks like a URI and resolves to nothing. The IRI is spelled out in full rather than as a CURIE because no context in this repo defines a Wikidata prefix -- the instrument block writes its Wikidata term in full the same way. (That one is the ENTITY IRI, https://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q3099911, since 2026-11-11; this one is still the /wiki/ page URL the stored records carry.)
Wikidata Q483242 "laboratory" is a subclass of facility (Q13226383), which is what makes it right for a schema:Place. An Organization type would not be: schema:DiagnosticLab is clinical and sits under MedicalOrganization, and schema:ResearchOrganization is an organization rather than a place.
This slot held nxs:base_classes/NXsource.html until 2026-11-09. That was wrong -- NXsource is the radiation or particle source that produces a beam, not the place it stands in; its name field conventionally carries a facility name, which is the likely route to the confusion. NeXus has no facility or laboratory base class, so unlike the instrument block -- where NXinstrument is correct and sits beside its Wikidata class -- there is nothing to keep here alongside Q483242. Bioschemas has no Laboratory type either; its LabProtocol and LabProcess describe the procedure and the run, not the place.
